summary: A red color made from cochineal insects. Many halal consumers avoid it because it is insect-derived.
halalWhen: Only if a trusted halal authority accepts the specific source and process
haramWhen: Listed as carmine, cochineal, or carminic acid without trusted halal certification
whatToCheck: Ingredient names such as carmine, cochineal extract, cochineal, carminic acid, Natural Red 4, karmin, or kosenil
Whether the product is halal-certified by a certifier that explicitly accepts this color
Whether the color is declared as insect-derived or hidden under natural color wording
saferAction: Avoid products listing E120, carmine, cochineal extract, or carminic acid unless a trusted halal authority explicitly accepts that exact certified product.
notes: Also appears as cochineal, carminic acid, carmines, natural red 4, or crimson lake.
A vegan label usually excludes carmine because it is insect-derived.
Only rely on it if a trusted halal certifier explicitly accepts the source and process.
reviewNotes: Reviewed as a high-confidence avoid record. E120/carmine/cochineal is insect-derived and should be easy for users to recognize under English and Balkan label names.
